note.text: Audience is the intended reader or listener. Purpose is what the writer seeks to achieve, such as inform, request, persuade or entertain. Tone is the attitude conveyed through wording and structure. A text can have more than one purpose, but an interpretation needs evidence. Formal language does not automatically mean anger; a friendly tone does not prove the facts are reliable.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to justify an audience-and-purpose reading using specific language choices. Builds on: main ideas and relevant details. Leads to: text types and directed writing.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original notice to pupils: Please return borrowed equipment before the club closes so that the next group can prepare. Ask the organiser if you need more time. The request targets borrowers, gives a reason and offers a response. Its polite, practical tone differs from an insult or a claim that a penalty has already been imposed.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Name the audience, identify the action or understanding sought and quote a short supporting phrase. Explain the tone through wording. Distinguish the author’s intention from proof that readers obeyed.

pick.q: Original line to club members: Please suggest a suitable meeting time and explain your choice. Which purpose is best supported?
e: The line asks for future input.
Its polite request contains no insult.
No result is stated.
pick.y: Please suggest and explain identify the intended action.

pick.q: Original appeal to readers: Support the reading corner; your donated books could widen its collection. Which interpretation is supported?
e: An appeal is not evidence of compliance.
No legal judgement is involved.
The wording seeks a contribution.
pick.y: The request and projected benefit support a persuasive purpose.

pick.q: Original message to a friend: I was relieved when your letter arrived. Which tone is supported by relieved?
w: Proof that all earlier worries were imaginary
e: Relieved conveys a different attitude.
The word expresses a personal feeling.
A feeling does not establish that previous concerns lacked basis.
pick.y: Tie tone to the actual word without inventing background facts.
